# slang

> A statically typed language built primarily for server-side and network programming -- that is the focus, not a limit. Compiles to C. M:N green threads, a precise mark-sweep collector, and native packages. Built and maintained by Dolphlabs (Dolph Tech Limited), https://dolphlabs.com.

Start with /llms-small.txt: the whole language on one page, about 3k tokens, enough to write correct slang. Every page on this site has a Markdown twin at the same path with a .md extension. /api.json is the machine-readable index of every package and function. /llms-full.txt is this entire site as one plain-text document.

## Pages

- [slang](index.md): A statically typed language built primarily for server-side and network programming. Compiles to C.
- [Language guide](guide/index.md): Values, types, and the shape of a slang program.
- [Data types](guide/data.md): bytes, lists, maps, structs and generic structs.
- [Errors](guide/errors.md): opt, result and fault -- and the rule for choosing.
- [Function values](guide/functions.md): Functions as values, deliberately without closures.
- [Concurrency](concurrency/index.md): M:N green threads, channels, select and mutex.
- [Testing](testing/index.md): slangc test, with assert and panic.
- [Benchmarks](bench/index.md): Every cross-language run, including the ones slang loses.
- [Packages](packages/index.md): The standard library, and how imports resolve.
- [C interop](interop/index.md): Calling C, and the safety rules that come with it.
- [How it works](internals/index.md): The compiler pipeline, the collector, the scheduler.
- [Limitations](limitations/index.md): What slang does not do, stated plainly.
